summary: Under `set -o pipefail`, `printf keyset | grep -Fxq` is negated with `!`. When the keyset is larger than the pipe buffer and the key matches early, grep exits, printf dies of SIGPIPE, and the pipeline status becomes 141. That reads as 'key not found', so a promoted entry is reported as unpromoted and the delete is falsely blocked.
failure_scenario: A mature ledger plus archive on the default branch gives main_keyset well over 64KB (hundreds of ~100-250 byte keys; this repo's ledger has thousands of lines). A branch carries an [open] entry whose key is already on main, near the top of the keyset. `git branch -D that-branch` -> grep -q matches the first chunk and exits while printf is still writing -> pipeline status 141 -> `! ...` is true -> the entry lands in branch_unpromoted -> deletion blocked with 'not yet promoted' for an entry that is on main. The agent wastes a retry or is pushed to the env-var bypass. It depends on a race and on keyset size, so it is intermittent.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:29 `set -euo pipefail`; :322 `elif ! printf '%s' "$main_keyset" | LC_ALL=C grep -Fxq -- "$b_key"; then`
suggested_fix:
Do not pipe into `grep -q` under pipefail. Test membership with a bash string match on a newline-padded keyset (`[[ $'
'"$main_keyset" == *$'
'"$b_key"$'
'* ]]`), or use here-string `grep -Fxq -- "$b_key" <<< "$main_keyset"` (no writer process to SIGPIPE).
needs_runtime_repro: Build a repo whose default branch has docs/found-issues.md plus found-issues-archive.md with ~2000 entries (keyset >200KB). Make a branch holding one [open] entry that duplicates the FIRST main entry. Run the hook with a PreToolUse JSON payload for `git branch -D thatbranch`, looped ~20 times. Expect exit 2 on some runs even though the key exists on main.

summary: Patterns 1, 2 and 3 require `git` to be directly followed by the subcommand. Git global options (`git -C <dir> branch -D x`, `git -c k=v push origin --delete x`, `git --git-dir=...`) therefore bypass the guard entirely. `git -C` is the usual form agents use from worktrees and scripts.
failure_scenario: Command `git -C /repo branch -D feature-x`. The gate passes (it has 'branch' and '-D'). The segment regex `git[[:space:]]+branch[[:space:]]+(.*)` never matches because `-C /repo` sits between `git` and `branch`. `branches` stays empty, the hook exits 0, and the branch with unpromoted [open] entries is deleted with no warning. `git -C /r push origin --delete x` is the same.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:113 `if [[ "$seg_cmd" =~ git[[:space:]]+branch[[:space:]]+(.*) ]]`; :139 `git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+(.*)`; :162 `git[[:space:]]+push[[:space:]]+[A-Za-z0-9._/-]+[[:space:]]+:(...)`. hooks/stop-reminder.sh:145 does handle `git([[:space:]]+-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)?`.
suggested_fix: Allow optional global options between `git` and the verb in all three regexes: `git([[:space:]]+(-C|-c|--git-dir|--work-tree)[[:space:]=]+[^[:space:]]+|[[:space:]]+--[a-z-]+)*[[:space:]]+branch`. Then run the later git commands with the same `-C` target.
needs_runtime_repro: Feed pre-branch-delete.sh a payload with command `git -C . branch -D <branch with an unpromoted [open] entry>` in a repo where `git branch -D <branch>` gets exit 2. Observe exit 0.

summary: Only the literal tokens -d/-D/--delete count as delete flags. Bundled short options (`-df`, `-fd`, `-Df`, `-vd`, `-dr`) fall into the `-*) : ;;` arm, so the delete is not recognised. The gate has the same hole for `-fd`: it contains no '-d' substring, so it exits 0 before the full path even runs.
failure_scenario: `git branch -fd feature-x` or `git branch -df feature-x` (git accepts bundled short flags). The gate lets `-df` through (it contains '-d'), but the tokenizer sees `-df`, falls to `-*) :`, and has_delete_flag stays 0. `-fd` never passes the gate. No block, and the branch is deleted.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:120-121 `-d|-D|--delete) has_delete_flag=1 ;;` / `-*) : ;;`; :146 same for push; :51 gate `fi_gate_gapped -d || fi_gate_gapped -D`.
suggested_fix: Treat any single-dash cluster containing d or D as a delete (`-[A-Za-z]*[dD][A-Za-z]*`). Apply the same pattern to the gate (e.g. a regex like `-[a-zA-Z]*[dD]`).
needs_runtime_repro: Run the hook with payloads `git branch -df b`, `git branch -fd b` and `git branch -D b` against a branch with unpromoted entries. Only -D blocks.

summary: Quoted spans are deleted from the command before the branch operands are extracted, so a QUOTED branch name is deleted along with the quotes. `git branch -D "$BR"`, `git branch -D 'feat/x'` and `git push origin ":$BR"` leave no operand, and `gh api -X DELETE "repos/o/r/git/refs/heads/x"` loses its refs/heads path. This is distinct from the known quoted-FLAG entry, because here the operand is quoted.
failure_scenario: Command `git branch -D "feature/x"`. After the sed quote-strip the text is `git branch -D `. has_delete_flag=1 but `targets` is empty, so `branches` is empty and the hook exits 0. Branch deletion goes through unguarded. Quoting variable expansions is the normal scripted form (`git branch -D "$b"`), so the common case is the unguarded one.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:92-94 `_fi_command_unquoted="$(printf '%s' "$command" | sed "s/'[^']*'//g" | sed -E 's/"([^"\\]|\\.)*"//g')"`; :129 `if (( has_delete_flag == 1 && ${#targets[@]} > 0 ))`; :162 and :167 match on `_fi_command_unquoted`.
suggested_fix: Use the unquoted text only to decide whether the verb tokens (git, branch, push, -D, --delete) sit outside quotes. Take operands from a tokenization that keeps quoted words (strip the quote characters, keep the contents), or run the operand regexes on the original command once the verb is confirmed outside quotes.
needs_runtime_repro: Payload command `git branch -D "b"` for a branch with unpromoted entries gives exit 0. The unquoted form gives exit 2.

summary: For Edit and MultiEdit only `new_string` is validated, and only lines starting with `- [` count as entries. A sub-line edit that flips status or appends an annotation is never validated, so the [fixed]-requires-token rule and the PR-format rules are trivially bypassed.
failure_scenario: Edit old_string=`[open] 2026-09-01 lib/x.sh:4` new_string=`[fixed] 2026-09-01 lib/x.sh:4`. new_string does not match `^-[[:space:]]+\[`, so it is skipped and exit 0 follows. The entry is closed with no verification token, which is exactly what rule 6 exists to prevent, and closures are irreversible. Appending `(PR: bad#5)` or a bare `PR #5` to the end of an existing line (old_string = the line's tail) also passes.
evidence: format-enforcer.sh:58-60 `Edit) content="$(get_field '.tool_input.new_string')"`; :84 `if [[ ! "$line" =~ ^-[[:space:]]+\[ ]]; then continue; fi`
suggested_fix: For Edit/MultiEdit, reconstruct the resulting full line(s). Read the file, apply old_string->new_string in memory, and validate the lines that changed. If that is too heavy, at least validate any line containing a `[open]|[fixed]|[deferred]` token or a `PR #N` fragment, not only lines that start with `- [`.
needs_runtime_repro: In a github-mode repo, send PreToolUse Edit JSON with file_path docs/found-issues.md, old_string `[open] 2026-09-01 a.sh:4`, new_string `[fixed] 2026-09-01 a.sh:4`. Expect exit 2 and observe exit 0.

summary: On every Edit/Write/MultiEdit of a non-ledger file the hook runs `$(cat)` plus two jq pipelines (7 forks, 4 execs) just to learn that file_path does not end in found-issues.md. A zero-fork builtin gate, like lib/hook-gate.sh gives the Bash hooks, preserves coverage exactly.
failure_scenario: Any Edit to src/foo.ts: `input="$(cat)"` (fork+exec), then `get_field .tool_name` and `get_field .tool_input.file_path`, each `$(printf | jq)` (3 forks, 1 exec). Only then does the `case` exit 0. On Windows Git Bash that is about 7 process creations per file edit, all spent on a decision the raw JSON text answers.
evidence: format-enforcer.sh:30 `input="$(cat)"`; :43-44 `tool_name="$(get_field '.tool_name')"` / `file_path="$(get_field '.tool_input.file_path')"`; :47-50 the late `case ... *) exit 0`.
suggested_fix: Read stdin with `IFS= read -r -d '' input || true`. Before any jq, `[[ "$input" == *found-issues.md* ]] || exit 0`. Both accepted path shapes contain that substring, and if the payload contains `\u` fall through to the full path. Then replace the two jq calls with one (or a bash regex for the flat `file_path` string).
needs_runtime_repro: strace -f -c -e trace=execve,clone,fork,vfork on the hook with an Edit payload for /tmp/x.ts, before and after the gate. Expect 4 execs to drop to 0.

summary: The Stop hook spends about 10 forks and 4 execs (cat plus three jq pipelines) extracting three flat string fields before it touches the transcript. All three can be pulled from the payload with bash regex builtins, as can the already-reminded early exit, on every turn.
failure_scenario: Each turn: `$(cat)`, jq for stop_hook_active, jq for session_id, jq for transcript_path. Each `$(printf | jq)` is subshell + printf subshell + jq. Then `tail`, awk, greps. That is the measured ~22 forks per turn, and on Windows a leaked token each. The common outcome is exit 0 at smart-fire (a conversational turn) or at the reminded-file check, after all the jq work.
evidence: stop-reminder.sh:54 `input="$(cat)"`; :66 `stop_hook_active="$(printf '%s' "$input" | jq -r '.stop_hook_active // false' ...)"`; :90 `session_id=...jq...`; :108 `transcript_path=...jq...`
suggested_fix: `IFS= read -r -d '' input || true`, then `[[ $input =~ \"stop_hook_active\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*true ]]`, and `[[ $input =~ \"session_id\"[[:space:]]*:[[:space:]]*\"([A-Za-z0-9._-]+)\" ]]` for session_id. Check the reminded file before anything else. Use jq only for transcript_path when the value contains a backslash.
needs_runtime_repro: strace -f -c execve counts for a Stop payload on a conversational turn, before and after.

summary: The grep fallback for transcript_path has no `|| true`. Under `set -e -o pipefail`, a payload without that key makes the pipeline exit 1 and the script dies with exit 1 instead of the intended fail-open exit 0. Exit 1 surfaces as a noisy hook error. The session_id fallback five lines earlier does have `|| true`.
failure_scenario: Stop payload `{"session_id":"abc"}` (or transcript_path null). jq yields empty, the fallback `grep -oE '"transcript_path"...'` finds nothing and returns 1, pipefail propagates it through `| sed | head -1`, the assignment returns 1 and errexit exits the hook with status 1. The next lines, `if [[ -z "$transcript_path" ... ]]; then exit 0`, are never reached.
evidence: stop-reminder.sh:14 `set -euo pipefail`; :110-116 `if [[ -z "$transcript_path" ]]; then transcript_path="$(printf '%s' "$input" | grep -oE ... | sed -E ... | head -1)" fi` (compare :96 `head -1 || true`).
suggested_fix: Append `|| true` to the pipeline at line 115.
needs_runtime_repro: echo '{"session_id":"x"}' | CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli hooks/stop-reminder.sh; echo $?  (expect 0, observe 1)

summary: Smart-fire inspects only the last 16KB of the transcript. Claude Code writes tool results as single, very large JSONL lines (the Bash stdout appears twice, in the message and in toolUseResult). Any turn whose last tool result exceeds about 8-16KB pushes the Edit/Write/Bash tool_use out of the window, so the hook concludes 'no substantive tool use' and skips the marker. The discipline silently turns off on the heaviest turns.
failure_scenario: A turn edits a file, then runs the test suite and gets a 30KB Bash result. The transcript tail is the end of that giant tool_result line plus the final assistant line. The awk finds no `"type":"user"` boundary, so last_turn is the tail, which has neither the Edit tool_use nor a Bash tool_use. `grep '"name":"(Edit|Write...)"'` fails, bash_turn_mutates returns 1, and the hook exits 0 with no marker required. The same 8KB window also lets a marker from the previous turn, or the literal marker text inside a tool result (for example after `cat`-ing this plugin's own hooks or docs), satisfy the later check.
evidence: stop-reminder.sh:178 `recent_tail="$(tail -c 16384 "$transcript_path" ...)"`; :194-198 `if ! printf '%s' "$last_turn" | grep -qE '"name":"(Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit)"' && ! bash_turn_mutates "$last_turn"; then exit 0`; :210 `tail -c 8192 ... | grep -q '<!-- found-issues-checked:'`
suggested_fix: Find the turn boundary on a bounded but larger window (for example tail -c 1MB), or scan the whole file with awk that keeps only the names of tool_use blocks since the last real user line. Restrict the marker search to the last assistant line.
needs_runtime_repro: Build a JSONL transcript: a user line, an assistant line with an Edit tool_use, then a user tool_result line padded to 40KB, then a final assistant line without a marker. Run with CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli and a fresh session_id. Expect exit 2 and observe exit 0.

summary: The first-run onboarding block runs `mkdir -p` and `touch` under errexit with no guard. If ~/.claude/found-issues cannot be created (read-only or sandboxed HOME, full disk), the hook exits non-zero before the sync or any ledger injection runs. That breaks the header's 'Exit code: 0 always' contract. Lines 128 and 189 are guarded with `|| true`, so the inconsistency is clear.
failure_scenario: A sandboxed or containerized run with a read-only $HOME and no existing marker. `.onboarded` is missing, so `mkdir -p "$ONBOARD_DIR"` fails and errexit ends the script with 1. The marker is never written, so every later session repeats the failure, and no open entries are injected. If only `touch` fails, the hint is printed on every session.
evidence: session-start.sh:13 `set -euo pipefail`; :99-112 `if [[ ! -f "$ONBOARD_MARKER" ]]; then mkdir -p "$ONBOARD_DIR"; cat <<'EOF' ... touch "$ONBOARD_MARKER"; fi`
suggested_fix: Use `mkdir -p "$ONBOARD_DIR" 2>/dev/null || true` and `touch "$ONBOARD_MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true`. Print the hint only if the marker write succeeded.
needs_runtime_repro: HOME=$(mktemp -d); chmod a-w $HOME; echo '{}' | CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT=cli hooks/session-start.sh; echo $?  (expect 0)

summary: Every SessionStart (startup, resume, clear and compact alike, since the payload's `source` is read but ignored) runs a full `sync` and a separate full `status` CLI process, even when the ledger has no [open] entries. The `status --format=plain` call is made BEFORE the 'nothing open, stay quiet' exit, so clean-ledger repos still pay for it. The statusline-migration check also runs jq, awk and sed on every session.
failure_scenario: A repo with a clean ledger and no [open] lines: session-start runs `$FI_BIN sync` (it loads the whole CLI and lists entries), `fi_entries`, then `$FI_BIN status --format=plain`, and only then reaches `if [[ -z "$open_entries" ]]; then fi_flush_codex_exit`. Each /clear or /compact repeats the whole cycle. With ~75 process creations per open entry, an ordinary ledger of 20 open entries is about 1500 creations in a hook that declares no timeout (hooks.json). On Windows that can run past the host's hook timeout, in which case the context is never injected. The `$(cat)` at line 337 is also dead, since `input` is never read.
evidence: session-start.sh:337 `input="$(cat 2>/dev/null || echo '{}')"` (unused); :366 `FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off "$FI_BIN" sync >/dev/null 2>&1 || true`; :375 `count_status="$("$FI_BIN" status --format=plain 2>/dev/null || true)"` precedes :378 `if [[ -z "$open_entries" ]]`; :245-249 jq/awk/sed on every session
suggested_fix: Gate sync on a builtin check that the ledger contains an `- [open]` line. Throttle it with a stamp holding the ledger mtime and HEAD sha, and skip it for source=compact/clear. Move `status` after the empty check, or derive the count from the already-parsed entries. Daily-stamp the statusline-migration probe like the nudge marker.
needs_runtime_repro: Count process creations (strace -f -c, or Git Bash procmon) for session-start.sh against (a) a ledger with zero [open] entries and (b) a stamp-hit second run.

summary: For each branch being deleted, the full main-plus-archive dedup keyset is rebuilt, with one `fi_dedup_key_for_line` per ledger line costing several `$(printf | grep | head | cut)` pipelines (about 20 forks per line). The rebuild runs even when the branch has no [open] entries and does not depend on the branch at all.
failure_scenario: Deleting a merged feature branch whose ledger is all [fixed]: branch_content is non-empty, so the loop builds main_keyset over every main and archive entry (hundreds to thousands of lines, about 20 forks each) before discovering the branch has nothing [open]. `git branch -d a b c` repeats the whole build three times. On Windows that is minutes of PreToolUse latency on a hook with no timeout.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:263-266 `branch_content=...; [[ -z "$branch_content" ]] && continue`; :299-308 `main_keyset=""; ... while IFS= read -r m_line ... m_key="$(fi_dedup_key_for_line "$m_line" ...)"` inside the `for branch` loop; :242-244 three `printf | grep | head | cut` pipelines per line
suggested_fix: First scan branch_content for `- [open]` lines and `continue` when there are none. Compute main_keyset once outside the loop, and only if some branch has [open] lines. Batch the dedup-key computation in one awk or bash pass instead of per-line subshells.
needs_runtime_repro: Time the hook with a 1000-line ledger and a branch with no [open] entries, and with 3 branches in one command.

summary: The git-commit and merge routes match against the raw command, including quoted text. The gate only checks for the substring 'commit'. A command that merely mentions `git commit` or `gh pr merge` inside a quote therefore triggers `annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto` or a detached background `sync`. pre-branch-delete strips quotes before matching; this hook does not.
failure_scenario: `rg -n "git commit" docs/` (or `gh pr create --body "... git commit ..."`, `git log --grep='git commit'`). The regex matches inside the quotes, no exit_code is present (read as success), and the hook runs `found-issues annotate-commit HEAD --hook-auto` against an unrelated HEAD. It can write (commit-auto: ...) suggestions onto entries and injects a misleading 'this commit produced annotation SUGGESTIONS' block. A quoted `gh pr merge` spawns a detached sync (hundreds of process creations).
evidence: post-bash-dispatch.sh:277 `if [[ "$cmd" =~ (^|[^A-Za-z_])git[[:space:]]+commit($|[^-A-Za-z_]) ]]; then`; :323 `if [[ "$cmd" =~ (^|[[:space:];|&])gh[[:space:]]+pr[[:space:]]+(merge|close|reopen)([[:space:]]|$) ]]; then`; the pr-create route at :240 is protected only by its `/pull/N` stdout check
suggested_fix: Strip quoted spans (as pre-branch-delete does) before testing the commit and merge routes. Require that HEAD actually moved, for example by comparing HEAD with a pre-hook sha or checking the tool_response for a commit summary line.
needs_runtime_repro: Run the hook with a Bash payload `rg -n "git commit" docs/` in a repo with an [open] entry whose path was touched by HEAD. Observe annotate-commit being invoked.

summary: pre-branch-delete.sh and format-enforcer.sh locate lib/ only via FOUND_ISSUES_LIB_DIR, CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT or a `found-issues` found on PATH. Codex user-level hooks (the only supported route since plugin_hooks was removed) set only FOUND_ISSUES_HARNESS. If the CLI is not on PATH, lib resolves to a nonexistent path and both hooks silently fail open. post-bash-dispatch and session-start derive the path from BASH_SOURCE and are fine.
failure_scenario: Codex runs `env FOUND_ISSUES_HARNESS=codex '/.../hooks/pre-branch-delete.sh'` for `git branch -D x`. CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT is unset (harness.sh says it is only a compatibility variable for plugin hooks), and `readlink -f found-issues || command -v found-issues` returns nothing. cli_dir becomes `.`, lib_dir becomes `./../lib`, the `[[ -f parse-entries.sh ]]` test fails, and the hook runs `exit 0`, so the guard is disabled with no message. In format-enforcer.sh the equivalent path leaves mode=local, so violations are allowed.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:209-216 `if [[ -n "${FOUND_ISSUES_LIB_DIR:-}" ]] ... elif [[ -n "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT:-}" ]] ... else cli_dir="$(dirname "$(readlink -f "${FOUND_ISSUES_BIN:-found-issues}" ... || echo "")")"; lib_dir="$cli_dir/../lib"` and :222-226 `# Lib missing ... exit 0`; format-enforcer.sh:160-172 same chain; compare post-bash-dispatch.sh:68,79 `lib_dir="${FOUND_ISSUES_LIB_DIR:-$__fi_hook_dir/../lib}"`
suggested_fix: Add the script-relative `${BASH_SOURCE[0]%/*}/../lib` as the first fallback in both hooks (as post-bash-dispatch does), and emit one stderr line when the lib is missing instead of silently allowing.
needs_runtime_repro: Run `env -i HOME=$HOME PATH=/usr/bin:/bin FOUND_ISSUES_HARNESS=codex hooks/pre-branch-delete.sh` with a `git branch -D` payload for a branch with unpromoted entries, with found-issues not on PATH. Expect a block and observe exit 0.

summary: The enforcer reads `.tool_input.file_path`, `.content`, `.new_string` and `.edits[]`. Codex edits arrive as `apply_patch` with the patch text in `tool_input.command` (and no file_path), so under Codex the hook will always find an empty path and exit 0. It is installed for Codex but does nothing there.
failure_scenario: Codex applies an apply_patch that adds `- [fixed] ... ` or a bare `PR #5` line to docs/found-issues.md. file_path is empty, the `case` falls to `*) exit 0`, and no validation happens. The install message and docs imply format enforcement on Codex.
evidence: format-enforcer.sh:43-50 `tool_name=...; file_path="$(get_field '.tool_input.file_path')"; case "$file_path" in *docs/found-issues.md|*.found-issues.md) ;; *) exit 0 ;; esac`; lib/codex-hooks.sh:118 registers it for matcher `Write|Edit|MultiEdit`.
suggested_fix: On the codex harness, parse the apply_patch text in `.tool_input.command` for `*** (Add|Update) File: .*found-issues.md` and validate its `+` lines. If that is deferred, document it as unsupported and do not install the entry.
needs_runtime_repro: Capture a real Codex 0.144.x PreToolUse payload for apply_patch (or confirm the field names from its hook schema) and pipe it through the hook with FOUND_ISSUES_HARNESS=codex.

summary: In `git` mode the 'passive warn' report goes to stderr with exit 0. For PreToolUse, stderr on exit 0 is not delivered to the model, so the advisory warning reaches nobody. The same applies to pre-branch-delete's 'promote-guard skipped' note.
failure_scenario: A repo with no GitHub remote, or with `gh` unauthenticated, has detect-mode return `git`. An agent writes `- [OPEN] ... - ...`. The hook prints the violation report to stderr and exits 0. The write lands malformed, and the agent never sees why it would later fail sync parsing.
evidence: format-enforcer.sh:189-192 `git) # Passive warn — emit to stderr but allow  printf '%s\n' "$report" >&2  exit 0`; pre-branch-delete.sh:200-204
suggested_fix: Emit the warning as PreToolUse JSON on stdout (hookSpecificOutput.additionalContext, or systemMessage) with exit 0, so the agent sees it without a block.
needs_runtime_repro: In a repo without a GitHub remote, make a malformed ledger Edit and confirm that nothing from stderr appears in the agent's context.

summary: All five hook commands interpolate `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` unquoted. If the plugin cache path contains a space (Windows home like `C:\Users\John Doe`, or a macOS custom config dir), the shell word-splits the path and every hook fails to launch. codex-hooks.sh already single-quotes the same paths for exactly that reason.
failure_scenario: CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT=`/Users/Jo Doe/.claude/plugins/cache/...`. The command string becomes `/Users/Jo Doe/.claude/.../hooks/session-start.sh`. The shell runs `/Users/Jo` with args, 'No such file' follows, and SessionStart, Stop and both PreToolUse hooks silently do nothing (they emit non-blocking errors).
evidence: hooks/hooks.json:9 `"command": "${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/format-enforcer.sh"` (also :18, :29, :39, :49); lib/codex-hooks.sh:87-95 `fi_shell_quote` exists because of 'an unquoted install root breaks on a path containing a space'.
suggested_fix: Quote the command: `"command": "\"${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/format-enforcer.sh\""` for all five entries.
needs_runtime_repro: Install the plugin to a path containing a space (or set CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT accordingly) and run the hook command through `sh -c` as Claude Code does.

summary: Without jq, pre-branch-delete (and format-enforcer) silently degrade to allow-all. `get_field` returns empty, so `tool_name` is empty and `[[ "$tool_name" != "Bash" ]] && exit 0` takes the exit path. No message is printed. jq is often absent in Windows Git Bash, the very platform the zero-fork gates target. The pure-bash gate has already extracted the command text but it is discarded.
failure_scenario: Windows Git Bash without jq. `git branch -D feature` reaches the full path, `get_field` prints nothing, tool_name is empty, and the hook exits 0. The guard that exists to prevent silent ledger loss is a silent no-op, with nothing to tell the operator.
evidence: pre-branch-delete.sh:57-65 `get_field() { if command -v jq ...; then ...; fi }  tool_name="$(get_field '.tool_name')"  [[ "$tool_name" != "Bash" ]] && exit 0`; format-enforcer.sh:36-40 returns `$default` when jq is missing, so file_path is empty and it exits 0
suggested_fix: Warn once on stderr (or a daily marker) when jq is missing. In pre-branch-delete, fall back to the gate's FI_GATE text as the command rather than exiting.
needs_runtime_repro: PATH without jq: run the hook with a `git branch -D b` payload for a branch with unpromoted entries. Observe exit 0 with no output.

summary: `git diff --cached --name-only | grep -Fxq` runs under `set -o pipefail`. grep -q exits at the first match while git may still be writing, so git gets SIGPIPE and the pipeline status becomes non-zero. The `if` then treats the ledger as 'not staged' and skips validation, so a huge commit sails through unchecked.
failure_scenario: A commit staging thousands of files (more than ~64KB of names) including `.found-issues.md` or `docs/found-issues.md`, which sort early. grep matches, exits, and git blocks on a full pipe and dies of SIGPIPE. Pipeline status is 141, `if` is false, `target` stays empty, and the hook exits 0, so a malformed ledger line is committed.
evidence: pre-commit.sh:18 `set -euo pipefail`; :28 `if git diff --cached --name-only 2>/dev/null | grep -Fxq -- "$candidate"; then`

summary: The injected-context cap does not bound criticals (`[!]`), which are always injected in full, and it does not truncate individual entry lines. A ledger with many criticals or long (suggested: ...) text injects an unbounded block into every session, resume and compact, on top of the auto-loaded rules skill.
failure_scenario: 40 `[open] [!]` entries at ~400 bytes each gives about 16KB (~4k tokens) injected at every SessionStart, and `slots` clamps to 0 only for non-criticals. The cap `FOUND_ISSUES_SESSION_INJECT_MAX=15` therefore does not hold.
evidence: session-start.sh:403-404 `slots=$(( max_inject - crit_count )) (( slots < 0 )) && slots=0`; :411-415 `injected_entries="$crit_entries" ... injected_entries+="$shown_noncrit"` (criticals unconditional; no per-line length cap)
